summary: Iteration 1 achieved a perfect score of 100/100 on the Maximum Clique problem using a branch-and-bound solver with degeneracy ordering and greedy coloring bounds. The greedy-only control scored 33.76, confirming that exhaustive search is essential. The problem appears fully solved.
key_points: h-main (BnB + degeneracy ordering + coloring bound) scored 100/100 — confirmed the hypothesis that BnB would score ≥90, and exceeded it by reaching the maximum.
h-control-negative (greedy by degree) scored 33.76/100 — confirmed the prediction of <50, demonstrating that naive approaches are far insufficient for this problem.

Key algorithmic insight: degeneracy ordering (processing vertices from the dense core outward) makes coloring-based upper bounds tight enough to prune the search tree efficiently. Without it, BnB only scored ~80.
Since score is already 100, there is no further optimization needed. Recommend approving and closing the campaign unless the problem set changes or new edge cases emerge.

If continued, the next iteration could investigate robustness: timing margins per test case, or alternative solvers (Bron-Kerbosch with pivoting, DLS tabu search) as insurance against harder future instances.
